title: Maximum Product Subarray
description:
Given the integer array nums, return the largest product obtainable from one nonempty contiguous segment. Contiguous means choosing indices from some start through some end with no gaps. You may choose a segment of just one element; you may not multiply an empty segment. The output is its numerical product, not the segment's boundaries.

For a segment ending at a given position, keep both the largest and the smallest product possible. Multiplying by a negative value swaps their roles, so discarding the smallest product can lose the best answer later. A zero breaks any continuing product but is itself a valid one-element segment. Compare against the best seen anywhere, because the winning segment need not end at the last element.

The array has at least one element. Negative numbers, positive numbers, and zeros can be mixed. Do not take the maximum over arbitrary subsequences: skipping a bad element would change the problem. With values [2,3,-2,4], the best product is six from the first two elements, not twenty-four from skipping -2. Values and lengths are limited so products used in the supplied cases fit the signed 32-bit range.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [2,3,-2,4]
Output: 6

Example 2:

Input: nums = [-2,0,-1]
Output: 0

Example 3:

Input: nums = [-2,3,-4]
Output: 24

Constraints:

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 100
  • -10 <= nums[i] <= 10
  • The product of every contiguous subarray fits a signed 32-bit integer.
